Basic Principles and Minimum Standards of Security 1.1 General These Security Regulations lay down the basic principles and minimum standards of security to be applied by OCCAR and its Member States, so that it is assured that a common standard of protection is established for Classified Information furnished or generated in connection with OCCAR Programme activities, and uniform practices are ap plied. Such Classified Information shall be distinguished either by a national classification marking or by the marking “OCCAR” together with th e ap propriate classification level. OCCAR - EA shall protect OCCAR Classified Information and national Classified Information received from its Member States in accordance with the provisions of this OMP . OCCAR - EA shall handle and protect Classified Informat ion received from other States participating in an OCCAR Programme or i nternational o rganisation or supranational/intergovernmental bod ies in accordance with relevant security agree ments or arrangements concluded with such states or international organisations . OCCAR Member States’ Government establishments and Contractors shall protect national Classified Information furnished to them in connection with an OCCAR Programme in accordance with applicable national security laws and regulations. 1.1.1 Principles of Security in OCCAR The principal objectives of security are to maintain the confidentiality of information by: a) safeguard Classified Information from espionage, compromise or unauthorised disclosure; b) safeguard important installations housing Classified Information from sabotage and malicious wilful damage; c) in the event of failure, assess the damage caused, limit its consequences and adopt the necessary remedial measures. 1.2 Personnel Security 1.2.1 Personnel Security Clearances All persons who require access to information classified CONFIDENTIAL or SECRET shall be appropriately security cleared by the competent national security authority having jurisdiction over the individual subject or legal entity to national laws and regulations and the minimum security clearance requirements set out in this OCCAR Management Procedure ( OMP ) . nd the minimum security clearance requirements set out in this OCCAR Management Procedure ( OMP ) . T he Personnel Security Clearance (PSC) for OCCAR - EA Staff Members and other personnel temporarily employed by OCCAR - EA shall be issued by the OCCA R Member State of which the individual is a national . P ersons without an established “Need - to - Know” to be employed in circumstances in which they may gain inadvertent access to information 20250801_OMP 11_Security Regulations_Issue10.1 – Page 15 of 73 classified CONFIDENTIAL or SECRET (e.g. security agents, maintenanc e personnel and cleaners), shall also hold a PSC at the appropriate level. 1.2.2 Security Instruction of Personnel All personnel employed in positions involving access to Classified Information as stated under para. 1.2.1 above shall be thoroughly instructed on taking up employment and at regular intervals on the need for security and the procedures for accomplishing it. Such personnel shall certify in writing , where required under national laws and regulations, that they have fully understood the security proce dures applicable to the handling of classified information and the possible consequences of non - compliance, which may be of disciplinary, staff contractual or criminal prosecution nature . 1.2.3 Security Status of Personnel Procedures shall be established to ens ure that, if adverse information becom

The equivalent security classifications of OCCAR and its Member States are shown in Annex OMP 11 - B. 3.2 Classification Principles Information shall be classified only when necessary. The classification of a document or material shall be determined by the level of sensitivity of its contents in accordance with the definitions given under para. 3.1 above. The responsibility for classifying information and for any subsequent downgrading or declassificati on rests solely with the originator . 3.2.1 Application of Classification and Markings Classified Foreground Information or Classified Information, which is generated in connection with any other OCCAR - EA
